  "text": "When the council removed the bench outside the library, Arthur continued to arrive at eleven with his newspaper.

For three days he stood beside the pale rectangles where its feet had been.

On Thursday, the librarian brought out a chair.

“We need it back by five,” she said.

“I’m usually finished by twelve.”

The chair was green plastic, with a split near one leg. Arthur folded his coat over the seat.

The following week, a woman with a shopping trolley asked whether he was leaving soon.

“Sports pages,” he said, holding up the paper.

She waited beside him. He read faster.

In November, the librarian found a second chair in the room where they kept the Christmas decorations. This one had arms.

“That’s yours,” Arthur told the woman.

“Why?”

“You’ve more shopping.”

They began bringing the chairs inside together. The woman held the door with her trolley while Arthur carried them through sideways.

A council officer visited in January. He photographed the pavement and asked who had put the chairs there.

“Temporary arrangement,” the librarian said.

In April, a new bench arrived, varnished brown and bolted to the ground. Arthur ran his palm along its back before sitting down.

The woman came at half past eleven.

“Plenty of room,” he said.

She parked her trolley at the other end.

Through the library window, they could see the librarian stacking their chairs.

“That green one wants mending,” the woman said.

Next morning, Arthur brought a small roll of tape. He left it on the returns desk.

“For the chair,” he told the librarian.

She put it in the drawer with the scissors."
